raw_response:
I am 64 years old. I have farmed these 8.5 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I never went to school. Everything I know, I learned from my father and from watching my neighbors. If Wang does something and his crop looks good, I do the same.

I have 6 mu where I plant wheat and then maize. The other 2.5 mu is for cotton. There are only two of us at home, so we do the work ourselves. I hire a tractor for deep ploughing because my back is old now. I have a well for water.

For the wheat: I plant in October. Last year I used an improved seed that my neighbor Wang bought from the dealer. His wheat had big full heads, so I will buy the same seed this year. For each mu, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer at planting — that is 50 kg. Then in spring, when the wheat turns green, I spread 20 kg of urea. At jointing time, I spread another 20 kg of urea. I irrigate four times: winter water before the freeze, green-up water, jointing water, and filling water when the grain is setting. I spray pesticide three times for aphids and rust. I rotary till the land after the maize comes off, then plant the wheat. Last year I got 500 kg per mu. This year I will do the same. I know last year I spent about 200 yuan per mu on fertilizer for the wheat, but I will not cut back. Better too much than too little.

For the maize: As soon as the wheat is cut in early June, I plant the maize. I buy hybrid seed from the dealer — 2.5 kg per mu. I put fertilizer in the planting holes, 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu. When the maize is up to my knee, I top-dress with 35 kg of urea per mu. I irrigate three times: right after planting, when the tassels come out, and when the grain is filling. I spray twice — once for weeds and once for the corn borer. I do not plough for maize. I plant right into the wheat stubble. Last year I got 600 kg per mu.

For the cotton: I plough the 2.5 mu deep in spring with the hired tractor. I plant my own saved seed, the traditional kind. Cotton needs more potassium or the bolls drop off. I put 40 kg of compound fertilizer and 15 kg of potassium fertilizer per mu at planting. Then I top-dress twice with urea, 15 kg each time. I irrigate four times and spray pesticide five times because the bollworms and mites always come. Last year I picked 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. I hope for the same.

Fertilizer costs more this year. The dealer raised prices. But I will not cut back. A bad harvest means I have no money for the whole year. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I can bear. I watch what my neighbors do. If Wang puts more urea on his wheat, I put more too. I do not listen to the young people from the county with their books and papers — I listen to what works in the field.
